::: {.why}
Interpolating a surface freely creates arbitrages; SVI restricts the shape so that a checkable parameter condition rules them out, which is a much better design than fixing violations afterwards.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- State the SVI parameterisation of a total variance slice and say what each parameter controls.
- State the condition on the parameters that guarantees no butterfly arbitrage within a slice.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Read the Gatheral and Jacquier paper's parameterisation and arbitrage sections and the second Imperial lecture, which covers the same material with pictures. The raw parameterisation has five parameters controlling level, slope on each wing, curvature and the position of the minimum, and the mapping from parameters to shape is the thing to internalise.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Implement the slice in qlib/derivatives/svi.py and reproduce the shape sensitivity: plot slices as you vary each parameter one at a time. Then implement the butterfly condition as a function returning whether a parameter set is admissible.
:::
:::
